thread.text: YOURE FULL OF SH*T

entries.whyItMatters: Border-radius has broken stronger people. Website reviews get emotional - better they happen in a comment thread on the staging site than in your client's inbox.

entries.headline: One comment. Six exclamation points. The entire review process on trial.
entries.hook: "I HATE THIS PROCESSSS!!!!!! nothing works!"

thread.speaker: Client
thread.text: I HATE THIS PROCESSSS!!!!!! nothing works!

entries.whyItMatters: Every agency knows this client. The extra S's are load-bearing. When feedback lives in email, this energy goes to your inbox - pinned to the page, at least you know exactly which part of the process they hate.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The process survived.

entries.headline: An all-caps meltdown about page layout, with a typo right in the middle of the rage
entries.hook: "WHY SHOULD I CHOOSE CLEAR ALIGNERS MAKES NO SINCE BEING AT THE TOP!"

thread.speaker: Client
thread.text: WHY DOES THIS PAGE STILL LOOK LIKE THIS? PLEASE PUT THE PROCESS AND BENEFITS CLOSER TO THE TOP OF THE PAGE. CAN I JUST HAVE ACCESS TO CHANGE IT MYSELF? WHY SHOULD I CHOOSE CLEAR ALIGNERS MAKES NO SINCE BEING AT THE TOP! DELETE IT MOVE IT TO THE BOTTOM.... GET IT OFF OF HERE.

entries.whyItMatters: Caps lock is how clients cry for help. "CAN I JUST HAVE ACCESS TO CHANGE IT MYSELF?" is the scariest sentence in web design - and the reason review tools exist.
entries.outcome: Resolved. Nobody gave them access.

entries.headline: A promo that needed to die, screamed about in two comments, ten weeks apart

thread.speaker: Practice staff
thread.text: PLEASE TAKE CARE OF THIS!!!!! (78 days later)

entries.whyItMatters: Every day that promo stayed live, new patients showed up expecting a deal the practice no longer honored. An expired offer on a live site is a pricing bug with a front-desk blast radius.
entries.outcome: Resolved, eventually. The special is no longer special.

entries.headline: The most decisive product feedback ever left on a dashboard
entries.hook: "COMPLETELY REMOVE THIS FEATURE!! WE WILL NO LONGER BE NEEDING IT!!!"

thread.speaker: Client
thread.text: COMPLETELY REMOVE THIS FEATURE!! WE WILL NO LONGER BE NEEDING IT!!!

entries.whyItMatters: No ticket, no user story, no acceptance criteria. Just a comment pinned directly to the feature in question, vibrating with certainty. Honestly? Clearer than most PRDs.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The feature is no longer with us.

entries.headline: A client declared war on em-dashes, in all caps, in 2025

thread.speaker: Client
thread.text: I am assuming this is changed with what you put in the product page. NO EM-DASHES!!! Missing frequency option.

entries.whyItMatters: Nothing says "this copy was written by AI" like an em-dash in 2025 - and clients know it now. Punctuation has become a brand-safety issue.
entries.outcome: Resolved - without a single em-dash. Except that one.

entries.headline: A dumpster rental company spelled "dumpsters" wrong in its own headline

entries.whyItMatters: One product. One word. The word is the business. When your entire company is dumpsters, "DUMPTERS" in the hero headline is not a typo, it's an identity crisis.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The dumpsters got their S back.

entries.headline: The primary CTA - the one button the whole site exists for - said "COUNSULTATION"
entries.hook: "BOOK A FREE COUNSULTATION" - the conversion button, converting typos

thread.speaker: QA reviewer
thread.text: Hero section - "BOOK A FREE COUNSULTATION" is a misspelling of word "consultation".

entries.whyItMatters: The hero CTA is the single most-read string on the page. A typo there doesn't just look sloppy - it quietly taxes trust on the exact button where trust converts to revenue.
entries.outcome: Resolved before launch. Counsult averted.

thread.speaker: Docs reviewer
thread.text: Well, crap. I guess we should give it more strict instructions and test whether that makes a difference

thread.speaker: Docs reviewer
thread.text: Do not modify, correct, rephrase, or normalize any part of the original text. Every character, space, and punctuation must remain exactly as in the source.

entries.whyItMatters: 2025 in one thread: an AI agent went rogue on enterprise documentation, and the fix was writing it a sternly worded prompt. Human review is how they caught it - the diff never showed up in any test suite.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The agent has been spoken to.

entries.headline: "Poof! Disappeared! Like a magic trick" - a typo that deleted every user's progress
entries.hook: One misread variable nuked ALL course data. The tester found out first.

thread.speaker: Beta tester
thread.text: I found a new issue! At this point, I should start a loyalty card. hehe. My dashboard is now having issues (these issues were not here like 5 minutes ago). I have lost all progress on all of my courses... they are all gone. poof! disappeared! like a magic trick...

thread.speaker: Developer
thread.text: I've been trying to get to the bottom of this one, but it's a real head-scratcher... I can't find any record of you having submitted answers for this group. Are you positive you completed lessons here?

thread.speaker: Beta tester
thread.text: This is not the course I tried to leave. And it happened to ALL of the courses on my dashboard.

thread.speaker: Developer
thread.text: I found it... The leave-group button is supposed to delete your data from JUST that group — but due to a typo in the variable, it couldn't read the group id, thought it was empty, and instead deleted the data for ALL of your groups. Whoops! Looks like you were the lucky one to try it first outside my test account... REALLY glad you uncovered this one before we launch.

thread.speaker: Beta tester
thread.text: Not a problem at all! Glad you were able to find the problem!!

entries.whyItMatters: A one-variable typo turned "leave group" into "delete everything." In production, that's a company-ending support week. In staging, with a patient beta tester, it's a war story with a happy ending.
entries.outcome: Resolved before launch. The tester deserves that loyalty card.

site.descriptor: Our own marketing site. We're not proud.

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (Spell Check)

finding.title: Typo in product name: Duperflow
finding.description: The product name is misspelled as 'Duperflow'. The correct spelling is 'Superflow'.

entries.whyItMatters: We built an agent to catch typos, pointed it at our own site, and it immediately found our own name spelled wrong. Deeply embarrassing. Also the best product demo we've ever run.
entries.outcome: Resolved in minutes. "Duperflow" lives on only in this museum.

entries.headline: The dentist heading up the practice, according to the homepage: "Dr. First Last Name"
entries.hook: A template string almost introduced patients to Dr. First Last Name, DDS

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (Lorem Ipsum)
thread.text: Template name placeholder: The text 'Dr. First Last Name' is a default template string used instead of the actual dentist's name. — Suggestion: Replace with the doctor's full name.

finding.title: Template name placeholder
finding.description: The text 'Dr. First Last Name' is a default template string used instead of the actual dentist's name.
finding.suggestion: Replace with the doctor's full name.

entries.whyItMatters: Template placeholders are invisible to the people who've stared at the site for weeks - and glaring to every first-time visitor. "Dr. First Last Name" would have been the most honest bio on the internet, but not a great look for a real practice.
entries.outcome: Resolved before a single patient booked with Dr. Name.

entries.headline: The page title advertised a different dental practice in a different city
entries.hook: Browser tab: Practice A in City A. Actual page: Practice B in City B.

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (Lorem Ipsum)
thread.text: Wrong business name in title: The title lists a different practice in a different city than the one this page is for. — Suggestion: Update the title and metadata to match the correct practice and location.

finding.title: Wrong business name in title
finding.description: The page <title> named an entirely different dental practice in a different city - a leftover from the template the page was cloned from.
finding.suggestion: Update the title and metadata to match the correct practice and location.

entries.whyItMatters: Cloned templates leak. The <title> tag is what Google shows, what the browser tab shows, and what nobody on the team ever looks at. This practice was quietly running ads for a competitor two states away.
entries.outcome: Resolved. Each dentist now advertises themselves.

site.descriptor: Our own web app. Again: not proud.

entries.headline: Our performance agent measured our own onboarding page. The number was so bad we published it.
entries.hook: First Contentful Paint on our own new-project page: 146 seconds. Limit: 3.

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (Lighthouse)
thread.text: FCP Poor on Desktop (146.1s): Desktop FCP is 146.1s, above the 3.0s limit. First content takes too long to appear. — Suggestion: Remove blocking assets and speed up initial server response time.

finding.title: FCP Poor on Desktop (146.1s)
finding.description: Desktop First Contentful Paint measured at 146.1s on our own onboarding flow, far above the 3.0s threshold.

entries.headline: A live medical site had a button whose label was "Add New Button"
entries.hook: The CMS asked someone to name the button. Nobody ever did.

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (Lorem Ipsum)

entries.outcome: Resolved. The button finally got a name.

entries.headline: Services offered, per the homepage: "First Service", "Second Service", "Third Service"
entries.hook: A full menu of services, none of which exist

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (Lorem Ipsum)
thread.text: Repeated service patterns: Generic 'First Service', 'Second Service', and 'Third Service' labels are used for the service cards. — Suggestion: Use the names of the actual dental services offered.

finding.title: Repeated service patterns
finding.description: Generic 'First Service', 'Second Service', and 'Third Service' labels are used for the service cards instead of actual services.
finding.suggestion: Use the names of the actual dental services offered.

entries.whyItMatters: Template cards are seductive: the layout looks finished, so the brain files the page as done. Meanwhile the content says nothing at all, in triplicate.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The services now have names, and probably prices.

entries.headline: The Book Now button - the one button the business runs on - linked to "#"
entries.hook: Header CTA: dead. Footer CTA: also dead. Main conversion path: a hash symbol.

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (Agency Reviewer)

finding.title: Book Now button links nowhere
finding.description: The Book Now CTA in both header and footer points to "#" instead of the booking URL - the page's main conversion action was dead.
finding.suggestion: Wire up the correct booking/scheduling URL for all Book Now buttons.

entries.headline: The privacy policy link went to a completely different dental office's website
entries.hook: "Your privacy matters to us" → *links to another practice's legal docs*

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (Lorem Ipsum)
thread.text: Mismatched privacy policy link: The privacy link goes to a different dental office's website. — Suggestion: Update the link to point to this practice's own privacy policy.

finding.title: Mismatched privacy policy link
finding.description: The privacy policy link pointed at a different dental practice's website - inherited from the template the page was built from.
finding.suggestion: Update the link to point to this practice's own privacy policy.

entries.whyItMatters: Legally, your privacy policy is a promise. This page was promising patients that a different business, in a different state, would protect their data. Template reuse without a final sweep = compliance roulette.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The practice now makes its own promises.

entries.headline: The doctor's bio read: Dr. David "Dr. Daviee" Do - a nickname inside a name
entries.hook: Is it a placeholder? A real nickname? The agent wasn't sure either - 60% confidence, flagged anyway.

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (Agency Reviewer)
thread.text: Odd nickname formatting in doctor's name: "Dr. David 'Dr. Daviee' Do" reads like an unfinished placeholder — confirm this is the intended display name. — Suggestion: Confirm the correct name/nickname formatting with the client.

finding.title: Odd nickname formatting in doctor's name
finding.description: "Dr. David 'Dr. Daviee' Do" reads like an unfinished placeholder - possibly real, possibly a template artifact.
finding.suggestion: Confirm the correct name/nickname formatting with the client.

entries.whyItMatters: The best reviews flag the weird stuff with humility. Maybe the doctor really does go by "Dr. Daviee." Maybe someone pasted a name field into a name field. Either way: worth one human glance before launch - which is exactly what the agent asked for.
entries.outcome: Open, pending a verdict from Dr. Daviee himself.

site.descriptor: Our own homepage redesign, pre-launch. Yes, again.

entries.headline: Our SEO agent audited our new homepage draft: no meta title, no JSON-LD. Zero for two.
entries.hook: The company that sells website reviews forgot the <title> tag on its own redesign

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (SEO Checker)
thread.text: Missing Meta Title: No <title> tag found in <head>. Without a title, search engines have no clear name for this page, hurting rankings and click-through rates.

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (SEO Checker)
thread.text: Missing JSON-LD Structured Data: No <script type="application/ld+json"> found. Structured data helps search engines understand page context and can enable rich results.

finding.title: Missing JSON-LD Structured Data
finding.description: No <script type="application/ld+json"> found on the page. Structured data helps search engines understand page context and can enable rich results. The same run also flagged a missing <title> tag.
finding.suggestion: Add Organization + Product JSON-LD and a proper meta title before the redesign ships.

entries.whyItMatters: A redesign branch is exactly where SEO regressions are born: the new page looks perfect, and the invisible layer - titles, structured data, rich-result eligibility - quietly ships empty. Our agent caught ours before Google did.
entries.outcome: Resolved before the redesign went live. Rankings unharmed; egos, slightly.

entries.headline: Every social share of this site renders a 215×34 pixel sliver instead of a preview image
entries.hook: Required: 1200×630. Actual: 215×34. Every LinkedIn share, ruined in advance.

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (OG Image Checker)
thread.text: OG image is 215x34. LinkedIn and Facebook require at least 1200x630. Upload a larger image or regenerate at the correct size. — Expected: 1200x630 — Actual: 215x34

finding.title: OG image far below platform minimums
finding.description: The og:image is 215×34 - a thin sliver. LinkedIn and Facebook require at least 1200×630, so every share of this page renders with a broken or blank preview.
finding.suggestion: Upload or generate a 1200×630 OG image so shared links render a real preview card.

entries.whyItMatters: Nobody on the team ever sees their own OG image - you see your site, not your site as a link card in someone else's feed. Meanwhile every share, forever, looks broken. This is the classic invisible-to-owners, obvious-to-everyone-else bug.
entries.outcome: Open. Somewhere, another sliver gets shared.

entries.headline: The headline said "Unlock Possibility." The AI-copy detector said: that means nothing.
entries.hook: An agent trained to smell AI-written filler, flagging a hollow AI-ish headline

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (AI Copy Detector)
thread.text: "Unlock Possibility" Is a Hollow AI-Style Headline: "Unlock Possibility" is a vague, overused AI-sounding phrase. It says nothing about what the event is or why someone should care.

finding.title: "Unlock Possibility" is a hollow AI-style headline
finding.description: "Unlock Possibility" is a vague, overused AI-sounding phrase. It says nothing about what the event is or why someone should care.
finding.suggestion: Replace with a headline that names the event, the audience, and one concrete reason to attend.

entries.whyItMatters: In 2026 the risk isn't broken pages, it's beige ones. AI-drafted copy ships fast and says nothing - "unlock," "dive in," "elevate." An agent that flags em-dash-energy prose before your customers roll their eyes at it is a very modern kind of QA.
entries.outcome: Open. Possibility remains locked.

entries.hook: A dentist found his service pages, word for word, on four rival practices' sites

thread.speaker: Practice owner
thread.text: YIKES..... the content on all of my services pages is on MULTIPLE OTHER [agency] SITES. [links to four other dental practices' identical pages] My content needs to be unique and not duplicated across multiple other websites.

entries.whyItMatters: Agency template reuse at its most awkward: same copy, four competing dentists, one very valid YIKES. Also an SEO murder-suicide - Google penalizes all of them.
entries.outcome: Resolved with a rewrite. The other four dentists remain unaware.

entries.headline: QA reported a 404. The fix suggested: "Turn on your VPN and connect to an American server"
entries.hook: The links only worked if you teleported to another country first

thread.speaker: QA reviewer
thread.text: Clinical Data and Resources - this link redirects to a page that does not exist. Please confirm and update

thread.speaker: Developer
thread.text: Turn on your VPN and connect to an American server to check these; they will all open. They are blocked for our Indian server.

thread.speaker: Second reviewer
thread.text: header still redirects to 404 error

entries.whyItMatters: "Works with a VPN" is a niche new genre of works-on-my-machine. The second reviewer's flat follow-up - still 404 - is QA poetry.
entries.outcome: Resolved, no passport required.

entries.headline: A French line-wrap debate resolved by a teammate calling himself an idiot
entries.hook: "Sébastien c'est un imbécile :D" - written by Sébastien

thread.speaker: Reviewer
thread.text: sur une seule ligne [on a single line]

thread.speaker: Teammate
thread.text: c'est Sébastien qui a demandé ça [Sébastien is the one who asked for that]

thread.speaker: Sébastien
thread.text: Sébastien c'est un imbécile. :D — En fait: desktop sur une ligne ça me va aussi. Sur mobile par contre, pas trop le choix que ça soit deux lignes? [Sébastien is an idiot. :D Actually one line works for me on desktop too. On mobile there's not much choice but two lines?]

entries.whyItMatters: Peak review culture: blame arrives, the accused turns out to be present, and he agrees with the blame. Line-wrap discourse transcends language.
entries.outcome: Resolved on one line (desktop) and two (mobile). Sébastien forgiven.

entries.headline: A five-word pricing review: "This app is crazy but $30 a month though???"
entries.hook: The most honest SaaS pricing feedback ever pinned to a page

thread.speaker: Reviewer
thread.text: This app is crazy but $30 a month though???

entries.whyItMatters: Compliment, objection, and three question marks in one breath - the entire psychology of SaaS pricing in eleven words.
entries.outcome: Open. The eternal question remains eternal.

entries.headline: One teammate's photo took over every profile on the team page
entries.hook: "I still can't get her picture out of every team member profile :-("

thread.speaker: Team member
thread.text: additional members are missing

thread.speaker: Site editor
thread.text: yes, I don't know how to add them. will need help.

thread.speaker: Site editor
thread.text: can you show me how to add team members?

thread.speaker: Site editor
thread.text: I figured out how to add folks, but I still can't get [one teammate]'s picture out of every team member profile. :-(

entries.whyItMatters: CMS default-image bugs create accidental monarchies: one face, every bio. The about page briefly implied the entire company was one person, which for a biotech is a bold claim.
entries.outcome: Resolved. Everyone got their face back.

entries.headline: The homepage testimonial video was for a completely different dental practice
entries.hook: The video player's own title gave it away - wrong practice, wrong state

thread.speaker: Superflow Agent (Agency Reviewer)
thread.text: Wrong testimonial video showing unrelated practice: Video player title references a different dental practice in a different state — this is stock/demo content, not this practice.

finding.title: Wrong testimonial video showing unrelated practice
finding.description: The embedded testimonial video's own title referenced a different practice in a different state - leftover demo content.
finding.suggestion: Replace with the practice's real testimonial video.

entries.whyItMatters: Testimonials are trust. This one was borrowed from strangers two states away, and only the video player's metadata knew. Agents read metadata; tired humans don't.
entries.outcome: Resolved before any patient noticed the accent didn't match.

entries.headline: AI-written SEO copy shipped with its own instructions still inside
entries.hook: Live page copy included "<!-- H1 - Primary keyword + location. Use once, at the top. -->"

thread.speaker: Content reviewer
thread.text: [pastes proposed page copy that still contains its own scaffolding:] "<!-- H1 — Primary keyword + location. Use once, at the top. --> <!-- 📷 PHOTO SUGGESTION: Hero image of the doctor consulting with a patient. Warm, professional. -->..."

thread.speaker: Content reviewer
thread.text: I am unable to edit on live site right now but this is a suggestion written with AI

entries.whyItMatters: AI-generated content arrives wearing its own scaffolding - HTML comments, photo suggestions, editor's notes. Paste it straight into a CMS and patients get to read the recipe along with the cake.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The instructions returned to being invisible.

entries.headline: One letter wouldn't change color on hover. The SVG had secretly drawn it twice.
entries.hook: "Bizarre. You won't believe it but the SVG had the C part twice."

thread.speaker: Designer
thread.text: Unsure why the 'c' isn't adopting current colour on hover.

thread.speaker: Developer
thread.text: Bizarre. You wont believe it but the SVG had the C part twice. See the two highlighted lines — when you put two on top of each other and make a transparent white it combines the two, making a darker white.

entries.whyItMatters: Two identical transparent paths, stacked, quietly doubling their opacity - invisible in the design tool, obvious on hover. The best bug explanations read like tiny detective stories.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The extra C was released back into the wild.

entries.headline: The button copy proudly announced: "THAT'S WHY WE OFFER OUR TEAM OFFERS"
entries.hook: We offer our team offers. The offers, we offer them. Team offers.

thread.speaker: Reviewer
thread.text: TYPO. "THAT'S WHY WE OFFER OUR TEAM OFFERS" INSTEAD: "OUR TEAM OFFERS LOTS OF GREAT AMENITIES TO HELP PUT YOUR CHILD AT EASE."

entries.whyItMatters: A copy-paste seam right in the middle of a sentence, shipped to a live page. Read it five times fast and it almost starts meaning something.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The team now offers amenities, not offers.

entries.headline: "In mobile this points right to ground squirrel's butt. Can we improve?"
entries.hook: A speech bubble, a squirrel, and a tail pointing exactly where it shouldn't

thread.speaker: Author
thread.text: In mobile this points right to ground squirrel's butt. Can we improve?

thread.speaker: Illustrator
thread.text: I don't think so. Solution would be to make a new bubble with the tail coming from the top left.

thread.speaker: Author
thread.text: New asset posted

thread.speaker: Illustrator
thread.text: top left! I'm seeing two versions, one with the tail coming from the lower left and one bottom right.

thread.speaker: Author
thread.text: Done!

entries.whyItMatters: Responsive design means your speech bubble's tail lands somewhere different at every breakpoint - and on mobile, it found the worst possible landing zone. For a children's book, a genuinely urgent fix.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The squirrel's dignity was restored.

entries.headline: "MAJOR GLITCH ON MOBILE: text on input fields auto-deletes" - with video proof
entries.hook: You type. The form erases you. You type again. It erases you again.

thread.speaker: Agency reviewer
thread.text: MAJOR GLITCH ON MOBILE: text on input fields auto-deletes — video attached

entries.whyItMatters: A registration form that deletes what users type is a 100% conversion killer that desktop QA will never see. The screen recording turned a "can't reproduce" into a same-day fix.
entries.outcome: Resolved. The form now keeps what you give it.

entries.headline: The broken "create account" link was fixed - by removing the link entirely
entries.hook: Bug: link goes nowhere. Fix: now there's no link. Task failed successfully.

thread.speaker: Client
thread.text: create account is broken and doesn't link to anything

thread.speaker: Client
thread.text: create account link is now missing

thread.speaker: Developer
thread.text: User will only create account when he purchases a product (that's how it was planned)

thread.speaker: Client
thread.text: User should be able to create an account either way, not sure why that would be a restriction…

entries.whyItMatters: Deleting the feature does technically clear the bug report. The retroactive "that's how it was planned" is a masterclass in scope re-negotiation via comment thread.
entries.outcome: Open. Philosophically, perhaps forever.

entries.headline: A $70 product's Buy Now button 404'd. The reply: "in livesite is also 404"
entries.hook: The staging bug that turned out to be a production feature

thread.speaker: QA reviewer
thread.text: HydraSmooth™ $70 - Buy Now - 404

thread.speaker: Developer
thread.text: in livesite is also 404

entries.whyItMatters: "It's broken in production too" is documentation, not a defense. Every day that button 404'd, seventy dollars walked out the door per person who clicked it.
entries.outcome: Resolved. Buy Now finally sells things.

entries.headline: Our own page said "swtich" instead of "switch" - caught in our own review
entries.hook: "Quickly swtich between versions" - quickly, but not correctly

thread.speaker: Team member
thread.text: "Quickly switch between different versions of the SDK"

thread.speaker: Team member
thread.text: The "swtich" is currently misspelled

entries.whyItMatters: We sell review tooling and still fat-fingered "switch" on our own page. The difference is it got caught in review - which is, awkwardly, exactly the pitch.
entries.outcome: Resolved. "Swtich" has been swtiched.

entries.headline: "Gesundheitseinrichtungen" was too long for mobile. The word, not the section.
entries.hook: Dev: "The word is quite long to fit." Reviewer: "can you split it?"

thread.speaker: Reviewer
thread.text: "Gesundheitseinrichtungen" mobile abgeschnitten, siehe Bild [cut off on mobile, see image]

thread.speaker: Developer
thread.text: The word is quite long to fit, that's why it looks cut off.

thread.speaker: Reviewer
thread.text: can you split it for mobile? "Gesundheits-wesen"?

entries.whyItMatters: Localization QA in its purest form: German compound nouns versus a 375px viewport. The viewport never wins without a hyphen. English-only testing will never catch this class of bug.
entries.outcome: Resolved, with hyphens. The word remains magnificent.

samples.headline: No llms.txt - AI assistants are guessing what your product does
samples.hook: ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity answer questions about your category. Without you.

finding.title: No llms.txt or AI-readable product summary found
finding.description: The site publishes nothing AI assistants can reliably ingest: no llms.txt, no machine-readable summary of what the product does, who it's for, or how it's priced. Assistants answering "best tools for X" fall back to third-party listicles - and cite your competitors.
finding.suggestion: Publish llms.txt covering product, audience, pricing, and FAQ pointers; keep it generated from the marketing site so it never drifts.

samples.whyItMatters: Search traffic is becoming answer traffic. AEO - being the source AI assistants cite - is the new page-one, and most sites haven't noticed they're invisible there.
samples.note: Illustrative example - the AEO agent is newly shipped, so this shows the report format rather than a customer catch.

samples.headline: robots.txt blocks the exact AI crawlers you want citing you
samples.hook: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot: all disallowed. Assistants quote your competitors instead.

finding.title: AI crawlers disallowed sitewide in robots.txt
finding.description: robots.txt disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot across the whole site - including docs and pricing, the pages you most want AI assistants to cite. Assistants now answer questions about the product from third-party summaries, which are stale and sometimes wrong.
finding.suggestion: Allowlist chosen AI crawlers for /docs, /pricing, and /blog while keeping private paths blocked. Blocking everything is a decision - make it on purpose.

samples.whyItMatters: Teams copy-pasted "block all bots" robots rules in 2023 and never revisited them. Three years later, that one file decides whether AI assistants describe your product accurately, wrongly - or not at all.
samples.note: Illustrative example - the AEO agent is newly shipped, so this shows the report format rather than a customer catch.
